title_html: Draft a company name using the pattern [City] + [Brand] + [Industry] + Co., Ltd.

items_html: The legal format is strict—e.g. Shanghai Acme CAD Design Co., Ltd.
Final name approval is part of filing; your agent can pre-check availability.

title_html: Secure a business-eligible registered address (commercial or approved mixed-use)—pure residential addresses are usually rejected.

detail.html: AMR requires an address that permits business registration with proper lease/ownership proof. Many cities accept approved mixed commercial-residential (商住/商办) properties or compliant centralized registration addresses—verify with AMR before you sign.

title_html: Get the landlord’s red Property Ownership Certificate (or equivalent) for the filing.

detail.html: Without this document, the AMR typically rejects the application.

title_html: Sign the commercial lease (deposits often paid personally or by your offshore parent).

detail.html: The tenant may not exist on paper yet; after incorporation and chops, the WFOE may reimburse allowable pre-establishment costs—confirm with your agent and accountant.

title_html: Retain a corporate services firm (WFOE registration agent) with a written scope—AMR filing, chops, and optional bank / bookkeeping support.

items_html: Before you sign, map your planned CAD/design activity against the 2024 FI negative list and sector licensing rules (see step 8)—construction engineering design often differs from general technical consulting.

Chinese law does not universally require a foreign founder to use an agent, but AMR online portals, templates, and local practice are almost entirely in Chinese—most overseas investors hire a firm to draft articles, run the AMR package, and coordinate chops and bank KYC.

Compare quotes before you finalize notarized / apostille packs: “incorporation only” vs. full-service (bank onboarding, bookkeeping, annual compliance). Tier‑1 cities often sit at the high end of quoted bands.
Government AMR filing charges are usually modest; the main cash outlay here is professional service fees.

title_html: Notarize your passport or parent-company documents with a notary in your home country (e.g. a U.S. Notary Public is typical for U.S. passport holders).

detail.html: Individual investor = passport; corporate parent = entity docs—your agent will list exactly what is needed.

title_html: Obtain an Apostille from your country’s designated Hague authority (e.g. a U.S. state Secretary of State for documents originating in the United States).

detail.html: For Hague Convention member states, notarization + apostille replaces PRC embassy legalization (in force for China since 2023-11-07). Non-Hague countries still need consular legalization. Provide certified Chinese translations of foreign documents—confirm the local AMR checklist.

title_html: Set registered capital and pay-in schedule in the articles—do not wire equity yet.

items_html: Registered capital (注册资本) is the subscribed total on the license; it is not the same as annual rent or payroll.
Under PRC Company Law (revised 1 Jul 2024), full pay-in within five years of establishment unless transition rules apply for older companies.

Before filing: confirm your planned activity against the 2024 foreign-investment negative list and market-access negative list; draft business scope with “（须经批准后方可经营）” where permits apply. Construction engineering design is separately regulated and often requires Sino-foreign cooperative design—distinct from general CAD/consulting.
Choose amount using: minimum viable for your sector, business plan, license minimums, banking credibility, and repatriation plans—align with your accountant.
Employer social insurance + housing fund is separate from this line—see step 9 and the dashboard.

title_html: Model a 12-month budget: rent, agents, payroll, and statutory “five insurances + fund.”

items_html: Pre-WFOE costs (lease, travel) often come from personal or parent funds; reimbursement after setup may be possible—confirm with your agent.
Payroll + statutory is usually the largest variable for a CAD shop—use the dashboard.
Assume onshore operating cash in China after capital injection (steps 17–18) and revenue.

title_html: Appoint legal representative, director(s), and (if used) supervisor—supervisor must be separate from legal rep/director.

detail.html: Legal representative and sole director are commonly the same person. If you retain a supervisor, they cannot also be legal representative or director. Under the 2024 Company Law, many small single-shareholder WFOEs may omit a supervisor by unanimous shareholder consent or use a board audit committee instead—confirm local AMR forms.

title_html: File the incorporation package with the AMR (lease + apostille + articles).

detail.html: Submit to the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR): lease, apostilled identity/parent docs, articles (capital, pay-in schedule, roles), and other required company rules. During online establishment, complete the foreign-investment initial information report (investor, UBO, investment transaction data) in the registration system.

title_html: Collect your Business License (营业执照)—the company legally exists.

detail.html: You still have no operational corporate bank accounts until steps 14–15.

title_html: Register and carve your company chops (official + financial seals—invoice chop usually not needed under nationwide 数电票).

detail.html: PSB + licensed vendor. A red chop on a contract is often decisive—secure storage; whoever holds chops controls signing. Carve an invoice seal only if you still use legacy paper invoicing or a bank requires it.

title_html: Open the RMB basic deposit account (基本户) with license + chops.

detail.html: Primary operating RMB account; statutory channel for wage/bonus cash withdrawals; payroll is normally transferred electronically from this account. KYC applies.

title_html: Open the foreign-investment capital account for inbound equity (FCY).

detail.html: Name varies by bank (FDI / capital account). Pairs with SAFE registration of the foreign-invested enterprise.

title_html: Prepare the bank’s capital-contribution / FX forms with your agent (投资款 wording).

detail.html: The remittance must be coded as registered capital—not an informal “transfer.” Codes differ by bank.

title_html: Wire registered capital from abroad in foreign currency to the designated inbound account.

detail.html: After inbound wire, the bank completes capital contribution receipt registration (货币出资入账登记) via SAFE’s capital-project system; obtain FX settlement documents only after receipt registration. Multiple tranches allowed within five-year pay-in (step 8).

title_html: Settle FX (资本金结汇) and move RMB into the basic account for operations.

detail.html: Follow the bank’s process; this is company capital settlement, not personal remittance.

title_html: Complete tax onboarding and enable fully digital electronic invoicing (数电发票).

detail.html: After nationwide digital invoicing rollout (Dec 2024), most new entities onboard via the electronic tax bureau—no golden-tax hardware required. You need this to bill customers compliantly on the mainland.

title_html: Register social insurance and housing fund unit accounts before hiring—optional to bundle at 一窗通 filing.

detail.html: You may tick “no” for社保/公积金 at setup and open later; there is usually no immediate mandate with zero employees. Once you hire, mandatory contributions are paid from the RMB basic account, funded by capital (steps 17–18) and revenue. Compare cities on the dashboard.
